exercises.instruction: choose the best option to complete each sentence.

exercise.body:
1) It’s 9 PM and Sam is [already / still / yet] working in the office.

2) I don’t live here [still / anymore / already].

3) Have you eaten dinner [still / anymore / yet]?

4) He hasn’t replied to my message [still / anymore / yet].

5) We used to go out a lot, but we don’t [yet / anymore/ already].

6) She’s [yet / still / already] gone to bed — she must have been tired!

7) My grandparents [already / yet / still] live in the countryside.

8) Is your brother [yet / still / already] living in Berlin?

9) They aren’t working on that project [still / anymore / already].

10) I’ve [already / still / yet] finished the book — it was amazing!

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct letter A, B, C, or D.

questions.question: What unforeseen results did the Flexner report have?

options.body: A) It caused the public to distrust the quality of medical education
B) It caused a dramatic increase in medical school applicants
C) It started a fierce debate over proper laboratory methods
D) It moved the focus of medical studies away from the humanities

questions.question: The writer lists humanities activities at Dalhousie Medical school to, show how these activities

options.body: A) Have become the most popular events on campus
C) Are of as high a quality as medical ones.
D) Have gained acceptance with teaching staff

questions.question: How do students at Dalhousie Medical school react to humanities activities?

options.body: A) They have difficulty letting go of the mind-set that scientific knowledge is more legitimate.
B) They report feeling that medical school has become more engaging and satisfying.
C) They have started to transfer creative ideas to their scientific and laboratory studies.
D) They have trouble connecting to talents that had valued before entering medical school.

questions.question: What is the writer’s main conclusion?

options.body: A) Greater emphasis on humanities in medical schools will benefit both patients and practitioners.
B) Medical schools are not adequately preparing students to become balanced medical professionals.
C) Creating a humanities program in a medical school is an overwhelmingly difficult but necessary task.
D) Medical schools should return to the early twentieth-century model of medical education.
